audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Quinn levels 2 and 3, first item and two items, and gave level 1 to 'Skill' — while the prose says level 1 'is hers', level 2 is 'Skill window', level 3 onward is Aurora's poke war and the two-item row is a skill matchup.
audit.why: Every row of the packet chart [Quinn, Skill, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Skill] matches a whys[] line already on the page; the shipped chart matched none of them. Win rate 53.03% over 66 games supports the version where Aurora owns the middle of the lane.
audit.corrected: Chart rebuilt to the packet chart in both layers with ratings aligned.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings describe Vault as a knockback that blinds you — 'Vault (E) you back with the knockback-and-blind', 'she'll knock you back and blind you', 'her Vault knockback'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Vault dashes Quinn to an enemy, damages and slows the target, briefly interrupts it, and lands her near her maximum attack range away. It moves Quinn, not you, and it does not blind — the blind is Blinding Assault, her Q. Playing around a knockback that does not exist means mis-spacing every trade: the punish window is her landing back at attack range, and the danger is the interrupt landing mid-cast.
audit.corrected: All four rewritten as interrupt-plus-self-reposition, with the 12/11/10/9/8 cooldown; the blind is attributed to Blinding Assault.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings said Between Worlds makes Aurora 'untargetable to outside enemies' and lets her 'walk through walls'.
audit.why: Riot's text gives Between Worlds damage, a slow, and an area she can teleport across — no untargetability, no terrain traversal. The genuine interaction against Quinn is better than the invented one: Vault bounces her a fixed distance back, and if the rift is placed on her that bounce keeps her inside the slow.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the slow-versus-free-crossing asymmetry and the Vault-bounces-inside-the-rift consequence.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes said 'Quinn: Vault online, level 6, first item' — Vault is her level-3 point and level 6 was unexplained.
audit.why: Behind Enemy Lines is a map-speed tool, not a lane spike: at 6 her power is roaming, which is why the two-item row is about map pressure rather than duelling. Aurora's real spike is level 3.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to Vault at 3, Behind Enemy Lines roams at 6, first item; Aurora level 3, Riftmaker, 2-item.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heightened Senses may or may not reveal Aurora inside Across the Veil, and the page says nothing either way.
audit.why: Riot's text says Valor reveals a large area nearby, and the kit's derived flags mark the ability revealsStealth. Across the Veil makes Aurora invisible on landing. If Quinn's W reveals her, the escape is not an escape in this lane and every W line on the page is wrong; if it only grants area vision, nothing changes. This is exactly the sort of claim the kit file cannot settle.
audit.corrected: Not written — left the text alone and raised it as a question.

edits.before: Level 1 is hers — she's a ranged carry with Harrier nimble move speed and you only have Twofold Hex (Q) and no W leap yet, so don't try to trade, just last-hit and accept the Blinding Assault poke. The lane flips fast though: once you have Q-curse plus your E slow at level 3, recast your Q so the curse-pull drags the missile back through her even after she Harrier-kites the first hit, and let your Spirit Abjuration spirits heal the chip back. Respect her Vault (E) — if you facecheck or over-extend she'll knock you back and blind you, so poke on your terms and don't burn W chasing a kite.
edits.after: Level 1 is hers — she's a ranged carry with Harrier nimble move speed and you only have Twofold Hex (Q) and no leap yet, so don't try to trade, just last-hit and accept the Blinding Assault poke and its blind. The lane flips fast though: once you have the curse plus The Weirding's slow at 3, recast your Q so the curse-pull drags the missile back through her even after she Harrier-kites the first hit, and let Spirit Abjuration heal the chip back. Respect Vault (12s at rank 1) — it dashes onto you, interrupts what you are doing and bounces her back to attack range, so poke on your terms and never burn W chasing a kite.

edits.before: This is your window. Through levels 4-5 your poke, passive spirit healing and W cooldown all line up — you out-sustain her Harrier chip and zone her off CS while she has no way to punish your spacing. At 6, Between Worlds changes the matchup: drop the rift on her, walk through walls untargetable to her Vault (E) and Harrier kite, then W-leap in for the kill — and W resets on the takedown so you keep snowballing. Bait the Vault first if you can; once her knockback is on cooldown she has no disengage and your all-in is clean.
edits.after: This is your window. Through levels 4-5 your poke, passive spirit healing and Across the Veil's cooldown all line up — you out-sustain her Harrier chip and zone her off CS while she has no way to punish your spacing. At 6 Between Worlds changes the matchup: the rift slows her while you cross it freely, so Vault's bounce only carries her to the rift edge and still inside the slow, and then you leap in for the kill. Bait Vault first if you can; once her interrupt is down she has no disengage and the all-in is clean.

notes: Vault was described as a knockback-plus-blind in four separate strings; it is neither. The same 'Between Worlds makes you untargetable / lets you walk through walls' invention appears here as it does in Renekton and Riven — it looks like one generator template applied champion-wide, so a grep for 'walk through walls', 'wall-walk' and 'untargetable' across champ-data would be worth more than per-matchup fixes. diff/diffRating left at TRICKY 7.5/10 despite the chart and a 53.03% win rate, because the scale is inconsistent across this file and I had no safe basis for a replacement number.
